name: Amateur Science
purpose: A starting subject map for a Amateur Science YouTube channel. Categories organize concrete subtopics; each entry supplies an episode question, a research outline and a boundary for case selection. Counts follow the authored coverage, with no imposed topic maximum.

topics.question: Why does a control group not solve every experimental problem?
topics.coverage: Compare confounding, measurement and assignment in a safe example.

topics.question: How can a household measurement be calibrated without laboratory equipment?
topics.coverage: Use reference comparisons and acknowledge traceability limits.

topics.question: When do repeated measurements fail to count as independent replicates?
topics.coverage: Separate multiple readings from independent experimental units.

topics.question: How can a small experiment be preregistered before results are known?
topics.coverage: Record hypotheses, exclusions and planned comparisons.

topics.question: What can a null result establish in an amateur experiment?
topics.coverage: Discuss sensitivity, uncertainty and competing explanations.

topics.question: How can citizen-science observations be audited for sampling bias?
topics.coverage: Map participation, geography and missing observations.

topics.question: How did a GLOBE Clouds satellite-matching correction change the matched citizen-observation dataset?
topics.coverage: Use GLOBE?s version notes for the erroneous 0.15-hour versus intended 0.25-hour window and the reprocessed matches; distinguish a processing correction from changes to volunteer observations or proof of individual accuracy.

topics.question: How can plant-growth and evaporation experiments isolate a meaningful variable?
topics.coverage: Compare controls, repeat measurements and low-risk materials.

topics.question: How does a pendulum experiment separate timing error from a real pattern?
topics.coverage: Track length, repeated observations and uncertainty.

topics.question: What must an amateur experiment report so another person can repeat it?
topics.coverage: Include calibration, independent replicates, error bars and safety exclusions.

topics.question: How can a neighborhood weather network compare sensors fairly?
topics.coverage: Standardize placement records and instrument checks.

topics.question: How can a low-risk lens experiment separate focus from magnification?
topics.coverage: Control geometry and record measurement uncertainty.

topics.question: What should an open notebook preserve when an experiment changes midstream?
topics.coverage: Record original plans, deviations and failed attempts.

topics.question: What can an amateur observational study infer without controlling exposure?
topics.coverage: Compare sampling, confounding and appropriate questions.

technical.requirements: Use the actual system documentation, a worked implementation and measurements. Identify inputs, outputs, constraints, tolerances, failure conditions and the limits of the example. Do not provide hazardous construction or unauthorized access procedures.
source_leads: official versioned product or standards documentation
test reports and drawings with clear provenance

science.requirements: Use original observations or experiments, an appropriate scientific reference and the actual measurement method. Distinguish mechanisms, correlations, model assumptions, uncertainty and limits of generalization.
source_leads: methods papers and current scientific reference works

civic.requirements: Use the current official legal text, policy, procedure or public dataset for a specific jurisdiction and date. Distinguish written rules, implementation and lived access; give no personal legal or financial conclusion.
source_leads: official laws, rules and administrative guidance
audits, judgments and public service records
consented accounts from affected people and qualified specialists

overlap_policy: The following homes have deliberately related subject matter. They are navigation leads, not proof that the same question belongs in every bank. Choose one primary home for an actual episode and link it elsewhere. Where a subject appears in more than one context, retain the distinct case, population, system or interpretive question.
handoff: Keep the BANK ID in notes. Refine the research question with an exact text edition, jurisdiction, population, product version, place, time range or clearly labeled fictional premise.
Inspect actual sources; no source was verified by generating this map. Apply the existing registry planning and idea readiness process before project creation.
Choose a current registered angle only after reading its niche-specific scope. This initial map has not checked or assigned angle plans for these entries.
Keep Q1-Q42, CAT defaults, project snapshots, output locations and production gates unchanged. Catalog counts are not production or publication counts.
Review neighboring banks for semantic overlap and follow the existing Phase 1 claim-ledger requirements. Add qualified review when required by the production contract.
coverage_limits: This initial map does not exhaust the niche, its regions, time periods, named case studies, texts, technical variants or disputed questions. It has not performed source-feasibility checks, semantic duplicate review of every pair, trend analysis, claim verification or episode production. Expand any category freely after identifying a real coverage gap; add categories where the subject requires them. Preserve existing IDs when refining wording and allocate new IDs only for genuinely new proposals.

# Amateur Science Channel Master Topic Roadmap (Scratch to Advanced)
**Niche:** 414 Amateur Science (Math_Scientific_Methods)  
**Channel Language:** English (YouTube)  
**Target Audience:** Amateur Science Researchers, Domain Specialists, Documentary Viewers, General Public (Global)  
**Production Format:** 10 to 30-Minute In-Depth Documentary Explainer Episodes (600s–1800s, 75–225 Fixed 8s Scenes)  
**Execution & Sync Report:** [topics/414_amateur_science/TOPICS_COVERED_REPORT.md](./TOPICS_COVERED_REPORT.md)  

---

## 1. Channel Progression Strategy

This curriculum organizes the core disciplines of Amateur Science across four progressive tiers:
- **Tier 1: Amateur Science Foundations & Core Mechanisms (Beginner / Scratch)** — Core physical and conceptual fundamentals, terminology, primary mechanisms, and foundational observation methods in Amateur Science.
- **Tier 2: Amateur Science Methodological Deep Dives & Empirical Evidence (Intermediate)** — Detailed instrumentation, measurement metrics, classification systems, and documented case studies of Amateur Science.
- **Tier 3: Amateur Science Advanced Systemic Paradigms & Comparative Dynamics (Upper Intermediate)** — Complex systemic interactions, historical shifts, anomalous patterns, and comparative analyses across different contexts in Amateur Science.
- **Tier 4: Amateur Science Frontier Technologies, Global Impact & Future Horizons (Advanced / Masterclass)** — Emerging technological breakthroughs, policy frameworks, environmental and human impact, and long-term evolutionary projections for Amateur Science.

---

## 2. Topic Styles & Narrative Angles (32 Curated Formats)

## 3. Topic Catalog (Scratch to Advanced Curriculum)

### Tier 1: Foundational Frameworks
1. **The Architecture of Amateur Science: A Volunteer Observation Program**
   - *Question:* Which dated project made nonprofessional observations useful for one question?
   - *Key Focus:* Trace protocol, data, and credited contributors. Evidence base: original project protocols, calibrated records and metadata, validation reports, published analyses, citizen-science data guidance, and participant agreements.
2. **Amateur Science: A Citizen-Science Result Rechecked**
   - *Question:* What did volunteer measurements actually establish?
   - *Key Focus:* Read methods, validation, uncertainty, and publication. Evidence base: original project protocols, calibrated records and metadata, validation reports, published analyses, citizen-science data guidance, and participant agreements.
3. **Amateur Science: Volunteers behind the Data**
   - *Question:* Whose repeated classification or sampling work was essential?
   - *Key Focus:* Use contribution and credit records. Evidence base: original project protocols, calibrated records and metadata, validation reports, published analyses, citizen-science data guidance, and participant agreements.
4. **Amateur Science: Question to Record**
   - *Question:* How can one observable variable be defined and logged?
   - *Key Focus:* Specify unit, site, date, instrument, and consent. Evidence base: original project protocols, calibrated records and metadata, validation reports, published analyses, citizen-science data guidance, and participant agreements.
5. **Amateur Science: Bias in Volunteer Data**
   - *Question:* How do self-selected participants or uneven coverage affect inference?
   - *Key Focus:* Map sampling frame and missing places. Evidence base: original project protocols, calibrated records and metadata, validation reports, published analyses, citizen-science data guidance, and participant agreements.
### Tier 2: Methodological Deep Dives
6. **Amateur Science: An Unconfirmed Observation**
   - *Question:* What independent evidence is needed before announcing a finding?
   - *Key Focus:* Check calibration, replication, and alternative causes. Evidence base: original project protocols, calibrated records and metadata, validation reports, published analyses, citizen-science data guidance, and participant agreements.
7. **Amateur Science: An Affordable Sensor**
   - *Question:* Does a new device improve the accuracy or reach of one project?
   - *Key Focus:* Compare calibration and reference data. Evidence base: original project protocols, calibrated records and metadata, validation reports, published analyses, citizen-science data guidance, and participant agreements.
8. **Amateur Science: A Volunteer Finds a Pattern**
   - *Question:* How did a named contributor's observation enter scientific review?
   - *Key Focus:* Trace submission, verification, and credit. Evidence base: original project protocols, calibrated records and metadata, validation reports, published analyses, citizen-science data guidance, and participant agreements.
9. **Amateur Science: A Project Changes Protocol**
   - *Question:* What data comparability changed after a dated method update?
   - *Key Focus:* Compare manuals and old versus new records. Evidence base: original project protocols, calibrated records and metadata, validation reports, published analyses, citizen-science data guidance, and participant agreements.
10. **Amateur Science: From Field Note to Data Set**
   - *Question:* How are observations submitted, checked, corrected, and preserved?
   - *Key Focus:* Follow an actual project workflow. Evidence base: original project protocols, calibrated records and metadata, validation reports, published analyses, citizen-science data guidance, and participant agreements.
### Tier 3: Advanced Analytical Paradigms
11. **Amateur Science: A Crowdsourced Claim Corrected**
   - *Question:* Which measurement or selection issue changed a conclusion?
   - *Key Focus:* Use original and revised analysis. Evidence base: original project protocols, calibrated records and metadata, validation reports, published analyses, citizen-science data guidance, and participant agreements.
12. **Amateur Science: One Site over Time**
   - *Question:* Can volunteer observations support a trend?
   - *Key Focus:* Check consistent methods, missing periods, and external drivers. Evidence base: original project protocols, calibrated records and metadata, validation reports, published analyses, citizen-science data guidance, and participant agreements.
13. **Amateur Science: A Proposed Citizen Project**
   - *Question:* Which training, sampling, and data-management questions remain?
   - *Key Focus:* Treat design as conditional. Evidence base: original project protocols, calibrated records and metadata, validation reports, published analyses, citizen-science data guidance, and participant agreements.
14. **Amateur Science: More Data Means Better Data?**
   - *Question:* When does inconsistent sampling overwhelm a larger count?
   - *Key Focus:* Compare validation and bias metrics. Evidence base: original project protocols, calibrated records and metadata, validation reports, published analyses, citizen-science data guidance, and participant agreements.
15. **Amateur Science: One Observation's Journey**
   - *Question:* How did a report become a verified data point or rejection?
   - *Key Focus:* Trace dated review and response. Evidence base: original project protocols, calibrated records and metadata, validation reports, published analyses, citizen-science data guidance, and participant agreements.
### Tier 4: Frontier Systems & Interdisciplinary Paradigms
16. **Amateur Science: Pattern versus Cause**
   - *Question:* What alternative processes could create a reported correlation?
   - *Key Focus:* Specify plausible confounders and tests. Evidence base: original project protocols, calibrated records and metadata, validation reports, published analyses, citizen-science data guidance, and participant agreements.
17. **Amateur Science: Calibration before Collection**
   - *Question:* Which standard or reference check supports a volunteer measurement?
   - *Key Focus:* Record procedure and drift. Evidence base: original project protocols, calibrated records and metadata, validation reports, published analyses, citizen-science data guidance, and participant agreements.
18. **Amateur Science: From Local to Regional Claim**
   - *Question:* How far can one volunteer network's data generalize?
   - *Key Focus:* Map site density and time coverage. Evidence base: original project protocols, calibrated records and metadata, validation reports, published analyses, citizen-science data guidance, and participant agreements.
19. **Amateur Science: Field Sensor and Reference Lab**
   - *Question:* How do controls and environments differ?
   - *Key Focus:* Compare matched samples and uncertainty. Evidence base: original project protocols, calibrated records and metadata, validation reports, published analyses, citizen-science data guidance, and participant agreements.
20. **Amateur Science: Expected Noise**
   - *Question:* Which background variation must a project measure?
   - *Key Focus:* Use repeated observations and uncertainty interval. Evidence base: original project protocols, calibrated records and metadata, validation reports, published analyses, citizen-science data guidance, and participant agreements.

technical.requirements: Use the actual system documentation, a worked implementation and measurements. Identify inputs, outputs, constraints, tolerances, failure conditions and the limits of the example. Do not provide hazardous construction or unauthorized access procedures.
source_leads: official versioned product or standards documentation
test reports and drawings with clear provenance

science.requirements: Use original observations or experiments, an appropriate scientific reference and the actual measurement method. Distinguish mechanisms, correlations, model assumptions, uncertainty and limits of generalization.
source_leads: methods papers and current scientific reference works

civic.requirements: Use the current official legal text, policy, procedure or public dataset for a specific jurisdiction and date. Distinguish written rules, implementation and lived access; give no personal legal or financial conclusion.
source_leads: official laws, rules and administrative guidance
audits, judgments and public service records
consented accounts from affected people and qualified specialists

prior_initial_map.overlap_policy: The following homes have deliberately related subject matter. They are navigation leads, not proof that the same question belongs in every bank. Choose one primary home for an actual episode and link it elsewhere. Where a subject appears in more than one context, retain the distinct case, population, system or interpretive question.
handoff: Keep the BANK ID in notes. Refine the research question with an exact text edition, jurisdiction, population, product version, place, time range or clearly labeled fictional premise.
Inspect actual sources; no source was verified by generating this map. Apply the existing registry planning and idea readiness process before project creation.
Choose a current registered angle only after reading its niche-specific scope. This initial map has not checked or assigned angle plans for these entries.
Keep Q1-Q42, CAT defaults, project snapshots, output locations and production gates unchanged. Catalog counts are not production or publication counts.
Review neighboring banks for semantic overlap and follow the existing Phase 1 claim-ledger requirements. Add qualified review when required by the production contract.
prior_initial_map.coverage_limits: This initial map does not exhaust the niche, its regions, time periods, named case studies, texts, technical variants or disputed questions. It has not performed source-feasibility checks, semantic duplicate review of every pair, trend analysis, claim verification or episode production. Expand any category freely after identifying a real coverage gap; add categories where the subject requires them. Preserve existing IDs when refining wording and allocate new IDs only for genuinely new proposals.
